title: Machine-cleared merge holds — how real systems spell "wait for the reviewer" when the reviewer runs out of band
summary: Prep research for decision #2910 (amend the platform-decisions anchor #blast-radius-advisory-care-not-a-gate). The question is a mechanism question, not a wording one: when the reviewing panel cannot run inline in the merge path — because the resident drain daemon is deliberately de-scoped to spawn no agents (plateau-app:tools/drain-daemon/daemon.mjs:9, the 2026-07-11 red-team de-scope; NOT the #2391 concurrency lease, which #2572 and #2910 both mis-cited) — how is the wait expressed, and may it block a merge? Three findings, each new ground for this repo (the existing reports 2026-07-18-blast-radius-advisory-review-gating.md, 2026-07-18-human-vs-ai-review-cognitive-science.md and 2026-07-10-ai-code-review-best-practices.md settle whether to gate and who judges, but never survey how a hold is spelled, who clears it, or whether it is time-bounded). (1) A BOT-SET, BOT-CLEARED BLOCKING LABEL IS ORDINARY: Prow/tide's needs-rebase is applied and removed by a plugin with no human in the loop, and Prow layers a status context on top purely to explain the hold (the label is the state, the status is the message); Kodiak keys auto-merge on a label, Palantir Bulldozer uses WIP/Update Me as blocker/trigger, and Gerrit lets CI service users cast the Verified vote that submit requirements evaluate. The label is not the weak part of the design. (2) THE NON-LABEL ALTERNATIVE EXISTS AND IS WORSE: GitHub code-scanning merge protection is a ruleset rule, explicitly NOT a status check, evaluated against the code-scanning alert store — a merge gate reading an out-of-band reviewer's ledger. It blocks while analysis 'is still in progress' and has no timeout, and its best-documented failure (codeql-action#1537) is a permanent block waiting on a result that never posts. Gerrit cuts the other way and is the instructive case: its strength is that votes and submit evaluation share ONE store (NoteDb), not that the record is a database; Prow/tide splits decider from store and its own docs warn GitHub's merge requirements must be kept in sync with tide's — the known cost of the split. So going non-label buys nothing and costs single-source-of-truth. (3) THE BOUND IS REAL PRIOR ART AND ITS ACTION IS NEVER 'MERGE ANYWAY': plain GitHub required checks have NO timeout (an unreported required context blocks forever; the documented 7-day rule expires a success, not a pending), but every system that OWNS a merge queue has added a wall clock — GitHub merge queue's status-check timeout, with 'timed out awaiting a successful CI result' as a first-class removal reason, and Mergify's checks_timeout, whose default moved on 2026-06-29 from off to AUTO-computed as the p95 of recent successful CI runs plus a margin (derive the bound from what the clearer actually takes, don't guess a constant). In every surveyed case the fired timeout EJECTS AND REPORTS — GitLab drops a failed MR off the train and re-pipelines behind it, Mergify dequeues, GitHub removes from queue. None converts a timed-out hold into a merge. This reconciles with WE's own ratified removal of the merge-anyway timer (#2425, bornAs x30jq9n): what was struck was a clock whose ACTION WAS TO LAND ('landing unreviewed code on a clock is never the right failure mode', we:scripts/lib/review-escalation.mjs:2022-2024, pinned by we:scripts/lib/__tests__/gate-invariants.test.mjs:119) — a clock whose action is to escalate loudly is a different mechanism and is not what #2425 removed. Cross-cutting: the advisory-vs-blocking line in the prior art is drawn on FALSE-POSITIVE RATE, not on who reviews — Google's Tricorder findings are advisory grey boxes in Critique behind a <10% effective-false-positive inclusion bar measured by the 'Not useful' button, while the no-false-positive tier is promoted all the way to compiler errors; SonarQube's deterministic quality gate blocks while individual issues comment; GitHub's code-scanning severity threshold gates the confident tail. Nothing in the prior art treats 'a machine reviewer's verdict is a merge precondition' as the gated-risk-score side of that line — a bot-cleared hold is how the review is DELIVERED, not a score being gated on. Re-grounding of the shipped tree (2026-08-17) also corrects the item's drifted refs (producerReviewLabel is we:scripts/lib/review-escalation.mjs:658-662, not :307-311; hasUnclearedReviewLabel is :1394-1427, not :564-569) and records that the machine clearer is BUILT BUT NOT RUNNING — runAutoLandSeam has zero production callers, runnerShadowPlan hard-codes LAND_MODES.SHADOW (we:scripts/lib/review-runner-core.mjs:113), landMode is 'shadow' (we:scripts/lib/review-policy.contract.json:112-115), enforceFlipReady does not exist in the tree, no agreement ledger exists, and the converge daemon's launchd job was never installed — so today every scored park is in fact a human park. Recommendation: keep the label, bound the wait, and make the bound escalate rather than merge. Full grounding in reports/2026-08-17-machine-cleared-merge-holds.md.
